youtube.title: ascent — three notes from a cave to orbit, six eras, one pulse
youtube.description:
Six eras of music from one motif: the same three notes carried from a stone cave to orbit at a steady 108 BPM, as the instruments, harmony, room and density change around a pulse that never does.

The motif is 0 2 4. It grows a note or a leap per era, picks up a second phrase in the electric age, and in orbit the machine plays it upside down over an ocarina still whispering it the right way up. The climax is uneasy on purpose: phrygian, the flat second grinding against the tonic, a counting voice ticking off the bars. The rooms move with the eras, hall to plate to the small box of a capsule.

Written as text, rendered in the browser.

Chapters
0:00 Stone — the cave
0:35 Bronze
1:11 Forge
1:46 Electric
2:22 Digital
2:57 Orbit — the motif inverted

Play and edit this song in your browser at jonborchardt.github.io/strudel-bench — press play, drag a slider, change a note, hear it immediately. Nothing to install. 

Every song here is a text file. This one is songs/ascent.strudel in the repo, along with the harness that plays it:
https://github.com/jonborchardt/strudel-bench

strudel-bench is a live-coding harness where a song is a text file written in a high-level language: parts, sections, and twelve musical axes (density, brightness, weight, space, articulation and so on) that a phrase like "darker and more spacious" can move. Most of the code and the songs were written by coding agents working from a written spec, in the spirit of my blog, "always shippable, always improving":
https://jonborchardt.github.io/blog/

The video is not a screen recording. It is generated from the song itself: every hit in the music drives the animation, and the world it plays in is chosen from the song's own musical features.

Built on Strudel, the JavaScript port of TidalCycles: https://strudel.cc
Samples come from the public Strudel packs, each under its own license: https://strudel.cc/learn/samples/

prompt: the evolution of humans from monkeys to astronauts: six eras at one tempo, the instruments, motif, harmony and room evolving, an uneasy AI peak with the motif inverted

requests.ask: make a new song mapping evolution from sticks and stones to lasers and AI; instruments, melody and progress evolving; forge drums too loud and annoying; electric melody too similar to my other songs; orbit clips; the orbit pad breaks playback

changes.why: hall>plate>room>capsule rooms move from a cave to a spacecraft, one 108 bpm pulse throughout since density does the work
notes 0 ~ 2 ~ 4@2 the three-note motif on ocarina in a hall; the same three notes return under orbit
level .8>.35 a hammer grid instead of house: metal on the off-beats only, the sixteenth clank was the annoyance
pipeorgan_loud>harmonica the organ measured 38 dB under the mix; the harmonica sits at the front
notes rewritten off the beat with a fall through the sixth and the leading tone home, so the hook is not the demo's shape
level .6>.32 the clipping: the 909 samples peak at full scale and the downbeat sums past 1; drive .8>.6 too, which is placement and hat accents, not distortion
patch wide dropped, width .8>.6, articulation .2>.45 supersaw already has unison; the wide patch times jux times a long release broke real-time playback
notes the inversion of the electric line (d -> 7-d) on wt_digital, level 1.3 so the machine leads
numbers 1..8 one per bar the AI counting the bars

the metal kit carried the highs (3 kHz centroid, the top high-band share, 3 dB under the mix); the lpf at 4 kHz takes the shrill off the anvil and the metal hats; mix high-band share halved
the harmonica a little darker with it (register .6>.55 came with the word); measured alone afterwards it holds almost no high band, so the kit was the culprit

notes 6@2>6 4 with follow the held sixth lands a major seventh on the III bar (E over F); the sixth now passes to the fifth, a chord tone under i and III both; the same line in electric, and its inversion in orbit, move with it
